newsitem.title: USA: Airbus CEO sees Asia and Pacific market growth.
newsitem.headline: Airbus CEO sees Asia and Pacific market growth.

text.p: Total demand for new airplanes for the Asia and Pacific region will increase rapidly over the next several years, a U.S. official from European plane consortium Airbus Industrie said on Tuesday.

Airbus Industrie of North America chief executive officer Jack Schofield said his firm projects that orders for aircraft with a 400-person or greater capacity for use in the region will total about 1,400 in the next 20 years.
Schofield was speaking at an International Aviation Club luncheon.
Airbus is continuing work to develop a 555-seat airplane, the A3XX, to accomodate the Asia and Pacific demand.

Schofield said Airbus is discussing investment opportunities for the A3XX project with companies in Europe, the United States and the Far East, but declined to specify which companies Airbus is considering as potential partners.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
